Cuts-the-Old-Knot: Cuts-the-Old-Knot, before the gate, staff lowered, with no stones. Tells, in order: she knows who the player is and what they carry; she cannot open the gate without them. "How did your handler always know where to send you? Why was there sap in a fort with no tree (the jar of Jal-Veesa sap the player took from the store, thing.mn12.sap-jar)? Who did you think was behind the cellar door? And why did nobody warn you that we were here?" The Toh-Reel-Ka keep people in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth, feed them sap and make them tell their dreams; a dreamer sees what any tree has seen, anywhere, and through them the order sees the whole marsh. The moans were dreamers. She was one for nine years; Never-Writes-Twice kept the key, and her story that Cuts went mad on sap and killed her minders is a lie. The answer to the player's question: she seals each tree she drains so the order draws no sap from it for its dreamers and its dreamers cannot see her through it; under the sea there are no trees, so nobody saw her here. She never meant a tree to die of her seal, and some have. She grants the order its reason: no second Umbriel, the flying city that the An-Xileel called down on Lilmoth with Lilmoth's mad Hist in 4E 48, whose dead killed the city's people. But the Xeech-Leel, the party that has ruled Black Marsh since the An-Xileel fell and that made the Toh-Reel-Ka, took the marsh by being not the An-Xileel and now rule unseen through the trees as the An-Xileel did. The healing the player was sent to do is for the dreamers: a sick tree shows them nothing, a healed one shows them everything, and the stones "kept safe" mean only the order can ever reach the Eye. She wants the Eye lifted, which parts the trees, ends the dreams and breaks the order; many trees will die of it, with the villages under them, and she will not pretend otherwise. She asks the player to stand with her or fight her here (answers: topic.mn17-fight, topic.mn17-believe). Does: sets stage 30.

*** Journal updated: At the Kings' Gate ***
Journal: Cuts-the-Old-Knot waited before the Kings' Gate without stones, and told me what the order I serve is. The Toh-Reel-Ka are the secret warriors of the Xeech-Leel, the party that rules Black Marsh, made so that no tree could bring another Umbriel. They keep dreamers in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth: people fed sap and made to tell what the trees have seen, so the order sees the whole marsh. She was a dreamer for nine years, and Never-Writes-Twice kept the key. She seals the trees she drains so the dreamers cannot see through them. Used where it sits, the Eye heals every tree, and the dreamers see through them all again; lifted, it parts the trees, about three in ten die, and the dreams end. If I fight her, I take her tomes, staff and draughts, face the guardian alone, and cannot give her the Eye. If I believe her, she fights the guardian beside me and giving her the Eye stays open. Either way the choice at the Eye is mine. I'm to choose.
